nodes.description: CDK10 and cyclin M form a heterodimeric protein kinase. With cyclin M lost or truncated, CDK10/cyclin M kinase activity is deficient. Its known substrates include ETS2, whose proteasomal degradation it promotes, and the RhoA-associated kinase PKN2.

evidence.reference_title: Cyclin-dependent kinases and rare developmental disorders.
evidence.snippet: Since the majority of the other allelic variants consist of large deletions or splice site mutations likely to prevent cyclin M expression, it can be concluded that the CDK10/CycM protein kinase is deficient in STAR syndrome.

nodes.description: Knockout of Cdk10, the kinase partner of cyclin M, models loss of the CDK10/cyclin M complex rather than heterozygous CCNQ loss. Homozygous mice die after birth with growth retardation, skeletal defects and kidney and lung abnormalities, and their embryonic fibroblasts grow longer primary cilia. No Ccnq-deficient mouse is described in the cited literature.
